entries.name: novelanything
entries.description: Synthesize novel RGB and depth viewpoints with remote NovelAnything in the robot Ego Harness, using only RGB input from the middle head_camera with poses and intrinsics. No input depth is supported by this skill.

tools.name: body_stop
tools.description: Stop all motion immediately and hold the current pose.

tools.name: create_goal
tools.description: Create a persisted goal that keeps this session working across automatic continuation rounds. Use it when the direct human request is a long-running objective, even if the user did not say "goal"; not for single-turn work.

objective.description: The concrete completion objective inferred from the direct human request.

max_goal_rounds.description: Optional positive safe-integer limit on automatic continuation rounds.

tools.name: ego_camera_calibration
tools.description: Read fixed RGB camera intrinsics and camera_to_reference transforms into the middle head_camera frame (OpenCV x right, y down, z forward; translation in metres) without images or motion. Each camera has pixel K and dimensions. No absolute camera pose is provided.

tools.name: ego_capture_cameras
tools.description: Capture your left, original and right RGB cameras at one sensor timestamp without moving. Saves three JPEG images and a manifest in your workspace and returns their paths, pixel intrinsics K, and fixed camera_to_reference calibration in OpenCV axes, metres, relative to the original head camera. Includes gripper_pose from the same encoder timestamp, with gripper_to_camera transforms for all three views. Works independently of the console camera display mode. No absolute camera poses or synthesized views are provided.

tools.name: ego_explore
tools.description: Turn in place through a full circle to perceive your surroundings. Use it first in a new place or when an object you need is not in ego_state.

timeoutS.description: Maximum seconds to wait for completion (default 120).

tools.name: ego_gripper_pose
tools.description: Read your gripper-link pose relative to your base and all three cameras from current joint encoders, your body model and fixed camera calibration. No motion or image capture. gripper_to_camera maps gripper-local points (x forward, y left, z up) into each OpenCV camera frame (x right, y down, z forward), translations in metres. The gripper frame is the gripper link origin. Includes sensor timestamp, measured lift/reach and gripper_to_base. For a pose synchronized to images, use ego_capture_cameras and its embedded gripper_pose instead of combining separate calls.

tools.name: ego_observe
tools.description: Report what your camera detects right now (categories and distances). Your world model also updates continuously; use ego_state for the accumulated picture.

tools.name: ego_predict
tools.description: Predict the consequences of a skill before doing it. Returns a receipt with a risk score, the issues found (for example a target whose position is too uncertain to grasp reliably), and the planned motion. Skills: "navigate" (needs x, y, optional yaw in radians), "pick" (needs target), "place" (needs on: a surface, an open drawer to put the object into, or a larger bowl to nest a bowl in; optional offset [dx, dy] in metres in the surface frame; or at: [x, y] to put it down on the floor, optional yaw for its final heading in radians), "open" / "close" (needs target: a drawer; the robot pulls or pushes its handle and ends standing back so the inside is in view). Floor-standing objects such as chairs are picked from beside them, carried a few centimetres above the floor in front of the robot, and put down with at; while carrying them the robot needs more room to turn. Objects inside a drawer are only seen while it is open. If the risk is too high or the skill is infeasible, follow the issues (for example move closer and observe, or choose another spot) and predict again. An infeasible receipt lists blockers: entities in the way, whether they can be moved, and parking spots (parkAt) out of the way; clear a movable blocker first (pick it, place it at a parking spot), then predict the original skill again. A receipt can be run once and expires.

target.description: pick: id of the object to grasp; open/close: id of the drawer.

on.description: place: id of the surface, open drawer or larger bowl to put the held object on or in.

offset.description: place: [dx, dy] on the surface, metres.

at.description: place on the floor: [x, y] in metres.

yaw.description: navigate: goal heading; place with at: final heading of the object (radians).

tools.name: ego_query
tools.description: Find perceived objects by category (for example "cup", "table") and/or near another object. Matching uses each object's role (the scene-level reading of what it is) and then its category probabilities, best match first, so a sideboard partly seen and labelled "counter" is still found.

category.description: Object category or role to look for.

near.description: Id of an object whose surroundings to search, for example "e:3".

tools.name: ego_rgb_recording_start
tools.description: Start background recording of ONLY middle head_camera RGB at a simulation-clock FPS, with same-timestamp measured odometry, encoders and calibration. Does not move the robot. Start before issuing navigation with skill_run wait=false; let this recorder sample independently of model/tool latency, then stop after navigation completes. Do not approximate 2 FPS by repeatedly calling ego_capture_cameras. Recording stops at max_frames or fails visibly on missed samples.

max_frames.description: Recording frame bound, default 256; provider bounds apply.

request_key.description: Stable 8–128 character recording-start key; reuse after lost responses.

tools.name: ego_rgb_recording_status
tools.description: Inspect recording status, actual sensor counts, simulation timestamps and errors. Does not command motion.

tools.name: ego_rgb_recording_stop
tools.description: Stop sampling and finalize all queued middle-camera RGB evidence; cancel=true explicitly discards the recording. If status is finalizing, query status until terminal. Does not stop or start robot motion.

cancel.description: Default false: preserve evidence. True cancels recording.

tools.name: ego_state
tools.description: Read your current understanding of the world: your own position, what you are holding, the skill in progress, and every object you have perceived with its estimated position, position uncertainty in metres, size, what it rests on, and when you last saw it. Objects you have not seen are absent, and positions are estimates.

tools.name: exit_plan_mode
tools.description: Use only in plan mode. Present your plan for the user's review and, on approval, leave plan mode. The user may approve (carry out the plan from your next step) or keep planning — their feedback comes back in the tool result; revise and present again.

plan.description: The complete plan, as markdown, starting with a # heading that names it.

tools.name: get_goal
tools.description: Read the current session goal, including the id and revision that update_goal requires.

tools.name: interrupt_agent
tools.description: Ask a subagent to stop its current work. This call returns without waiting for it to stop. You can continue a local direct child's conversation later with send_message. External executions stop permanently and cannot receive follow-ups. Subagents it started will keep running.

agent_id.description: The id of an agent created under you: your direct child or a deeper descendant.

tools.name: list_agents
tools.description: List subagents you started, with their ids, labels, and status. running means it is working; inactive means it is not currently working. You will be notified when a subagent finishes; there is no need to keep checking its status. Use send_message to continue the conversation.

scope.description: children (default) lists direct children, which accept send_message in any status. descendants lists the whole tree below you with each entry's parent session id and depth; entries deeper than 1 accept only interrupt_agent.

tools.name: novelanything_download
tools.description: Download exact artifact paths from a successful result into outputs/novelanything/<job_id>, preserving subdirectories. Returns absolute files and local_manifest_path. Local SHA256 is recorded; server checksum verification occurs only when the server supplies a checksum.

job_id.description: Exact job id returned by NovelAnything; never invent identities.

artifact_paths.description: Unique nonempty selection of exact result.artifacts[].path values.

tools.name: novelanything_health
tools.description: Check hosted NovelAnything model readiness without inference.

tools.name: novelanything_log
tools.description: Read bounded NovelAnything server job log for failure diagnosis.

job_id.description: Exact job id returned by NovelAnything; never invent identities.

tools.name: novelanything_prepare_gripper_view
tools.description: Prepare a local NovelAnything ZIP from a succeeded ego_rgb_recording. Uses only recorded middle head_camera RGB, with no depth input, and derives shared-frame w2c from synchronized robot odometry, encoders and the robot model. The target is the CURRENT gripper link origin looking along gripper +X with image-up +Z, using middle-camera intrinsics. Returns archive_path and context/target indices; retains all sampled evidence in the ZIP. No navigation, general shell/files or inference. Upload the returned archive with novelanything_upload, then submit with returned indices and label the result gripper_view_prediction. If preparation is unavailable or fails, report that failure; never substitute rgbd_video_gen for an explicitly requested NovelAnything job.

num_source_views.description: Optional 2–16 contexts, at most recorded frames; omitted selects up to 16 across the recording.

tools.name: novelanything_result
tools.description: Read successful result metadata and exact artifact paths. Rejects every state except succeeded. Generated RGB and depth are predictions, not observations or motion clearance.

job_id.description: Exact job id returned by NovelAnything; never invent identities.

tools.name: novelanything_samples
tools.description: List server demo samples or inspect one before selecting frames. Samples are not observations of robot surroundings.

sample_id.description: Omit to list samples; otherwise use an actual listed sample id.

tools.name: novelanything_status
tools.description: Inspect or briefly poll a NovelAnything job. queued/running are pending; failed/cancelled/interrupted stop synthesis. Local timeout does not cancel remote work.

job_id.description: Exact job id returned by NovelAnything; never invent identities.

wait_seconds.description: Default 0: one query. Otherwise bounded by provider maxWaitSeconds (default 20).

tools.name: novelanything_submit
tools.description: Queue NovelAnything RGB/depth prediction from exactly one sample_id or upload_id. When the user explicitly requests NovelAnything, do not substitute rgbd_video_gen if preparation or submission fails. Set both context and target or neither (scene defaults). Context: 2–16 distinct indices with RGB and calibration; target: 1–6 distinct disjoint indices. For robot evidence, all context frames must be from the same middle head_camera at different timestamps/poses; never combine side-camera RGB or supply depth. Targets may omit GT. Returns acceptance, not completion. No automatic POST retry; UNKNOWN_OUTCOME must be reconciled by the operator.

sample_id.description: Explicit demo sample id; mutually exclusive with upload_id.

upload_id.description: Id returned by novelanything_upload; mutually exclusive with sample_id.

context.description: Zero-based context frame indices; omit with target for scene defaults.

target.description: Zero-based target frame indices, disjoint from context.

metrics.description: Default true: score only targets with GT of that modality. False disables scoring, not prediction.

request_key.description: Stable local request identity, 8–128 letters/digits or ._:-. Reuse after accepted replies. UNKNOWN_OUTCOME requires operator reconciliation; never retry with a new key.

tools.name: novelanything_upload
tools.description: Archive and upload a robot-workspace ZIP with root scene.json and posed RGB files, without inference. Robot RGB inputs must come only from the middle head_camera; depth inputs are unsupported by this skill; exclude head_camera_left and head_camera_right. Context needs RGB, OpenCV world-to-camera w2c and fxfycxcy; omit depth_path. Targets need w2c; no depth input or GT is used. A single capture or SLARM/rgbd_video_gen ZIP is not this format.

archive_path.description: Existing compliant scene ZIP beneath robot inputRoot.

request_key.description: Stable local request identity, 8–128 letters/digits or ._:-. Reuse after accepted replies. UNKNOWN_OUTCOME requires operator reconciliation; never retry with a new key.

tools.name: report_problem
tools.description: Alert the operator that you hit a situation you cannot resolve by yourself: an unexpected error, a skill that keeps failing, or a task that cannot be done from here. Before calling, review your own tool calls in this turn and diagnose: which prediction or skill failed, the error text, how often it repeated, where you were, and how it relates to blockers, uncertainty, or missing or duplicate objects in the ego state. The operator console shows the report as an alert. Call it once, then stop.

goal.description: What you are trying to achieve.

step.description: The step you were carrying out when you got stuck.

diagnosis.description: The cause you diagnosed from your tool log and the evidence for it.

message.description: What happened, what you tried, and what you need from the operator.

tools.name: rgbd_video_gen_cancel
tools.description: Explicitly cancel a job submitted or recovered in this local store. Stopping a chat does not cancel accepted remote work. Only cancelled=true confirms cancellation.

job_id.description: Actual j_ job_id returned by rgbd_video_gen. Never invent ids.

wait_seconds.description: Bounded wait in seconds, default 0 (one query); provider limit defaults to 20. Aborting polling does not cancel generation.

tools.name: rgbd_video_gen_capabilities
tools.description: Read rgbd_video_gen readiness, current defaults and limits. Does not run generation.

tools.name: rgbd_video_gen_demo
tools.description: Generate from a named server-installed demo, e.g. waymo080 or re10k_172c99489b18e0e6. No local images are needed. trajectory uses its target camera path; bev generates bird-eye poses and has no target ground truth. With bev, explicitly provide num_bev_views and bev_altitude_scale.

request_key.description: Stable operation key: 8-128 letters/digits or ._:-. Reuse exactly after disconnects or unknown outcomes; new keys create new work.

num_source_views.description: First 1-8 frames are evidence images; omitted uses current server default (normally 6). Explicitly set for fewer than 6 evidence images, e.g. 3 for a three-camera snapshot plus target poses. The model was trained on 6 evidence views; other counts may reduce quality.

max_target_views.description: Target view limit, 1-24; omitted uses server default.

num_inference_steps.description: Euler sampling steps, 1-100; omitted uses server default.

seed.description: Nonnegative integer random seed; omitted uses server default.

output_fps.description: Output video fps, 1-60; omitted uses server default.

bev_altitude_scale.description: Required for bev: positive height multiplier of the source camera horizontal radius.

tools.name: rgbd_video_gen_download
tools.description: Save under outputsDir and return local_manifest_path for downstream consumers. Download exact artifact filenames from a successful result (videos, frames.zip, depth.npz, comparison strip, meta.json). Verifies byte counts and SHA256 before publishing local files; retries reuse verified files. No arbitrary URL or destination path is accepted.

job_id.description: Actual j_ job_id returned by rgbd_video_gen. Never invent ids.

tools.name: rgbd_video_gen_prepare_gripper_view
tools.description: Build and save a generation-ready scene JSON from capture.json returned by ego_capture_cameras. Reads the three saved JPEGs and the same-timestamp embedded gripper_pose, converts gripper forward/left/up axes to an OpenCV virtual camera at the gripper link origin looking along gripper +X with image-up +Z. Uses the middle camera as the common reference and reuses its intrinsics. Returns inputRoot-relative scene_path, absolute local_scene_path, num_source_views=3 and max_target_views=1. No shell, file-authoring tools, subagent delegation or remote generation is needed for this step.

capture_manifest_path.description: Exact manifest_path returned by ego_capture_cameras; must be beneath inputRoot.

tools.name: rgbd_video_gen_result
tools.description: Read a successful result and save its manifest. RGB, metric depth and videos are predictions, not observed geometry. Target PSNR exists only with target GT. target_cameras[i] maps to pred_{num_source_views+i}.jpg, not always pred_{6+i}.jpg. Select returned filenames for download.

job_id.description: Actual j_ job_id returned by rgbd_video_gen. Never invent ids.

tools.name: rgbd_video_gen_status
tools.description: Query generation. queued/running are pending; succeeded requires result; failed/cancelled means stop and report error. 100% progress alone is not success.

job_id.description: Actual j_ job_id returned by rgbd_video_gen. Never invent ids.

wait_seconds.description: Bounded wait in seconds, default 0 (one query); provider limit defaults to 20. Aborting polling does not cancel generation.

tools.name: rgbd_video_gen_submit
tools.description: Upload a local rgbd_videogen_scene_v1 JSON scene with inline PNG/JPEG base64 images. Requires 2-64 ordered frames and at least num_source_views + 1 frames, known intrinsics and OpenCV camera-to-world poses in metres. First num_source_views frames provide evidence; remaining frames are target poses with optional images for GT comparison. Returns an accepted job, not completion. This sends images to the configured remote server. It does not estimate poses or accept SLARM capture ZIPs.

scene_path.description: JSON file beneath inputRoot; relative paths resolve from that root.

request_key.description: Stable operation key: 8-128 letters/digits or ._:-. Reuse exactly after disconnects or unknown outcomes; new keys create new work.

num_source_views.description: First 1-8 frames are evidence images; omitted uses current server default (normally 6). Explicitly set for fewer than 6 evidence images, e.g. 3 for a three-camera snapshot plus target poses. The model was trained on 6 evidence views; other counts may reduce quality.

max_target_views.description: Target view limit, 1-24; omitted uses server default.

num_inference_steps.description: Euler sampling steps, 1-100; omitted uses server default.

seed.description: Nonnegative integer random seed; omitted uses server default.

output_fps.description: Output video fps, 1-60; omitted uses server default.

tools.name: rgbd_video_gen_upload
tools.description: Upload a local ZIP containing rgbd_videogen_scene_v1 scene.json and its relative image files. Uses server generation defaults. Not compatible with world_capture slarm_scene_v1 ZIPs. Returns job_id; use status then result and download.

archive_path.description: ZIP beneath inputRoot, at most the configured upload limit.

request_key.description: Stable operation key: 8-128 letters/digits or ._:-. Reuse exactly after disconnects or unknown outcomes; new keys create new work.

tools.description: Send a message to an agent. A working agent receives it at its next step; an idle agent starts a new turn with it. Returns delivery confirmation, not the agent's answer.

tools.name: subagent

The subagent returns its result, not its intermediate steps. This tool starts an independently managed subagent and immediately returns its id. The runtime notifies you when it finishes. The child reports results with `send_message`; use `send_message` to steer it while running or continue its conversation after it finishes.

Use this when the subtask builds on this conversation's context — a follow-up analysis, a review, a continuation — without consuming this conversation's context for the work itself. You receive its result, not its intermediate steps. This tool starts an independently managed subagent and immediately returns its id. The runtime notifies you when it finishes. The child reports results with `send_message`; use `send_message` to steer it while running or continue its conversation after it finishes.

<skill_content name="novelanything">
<skill_resources>
Base directory for this skill: {{dshWorkspace}}/packages/dsh-bundle-novelanything/skills/novelanything
Resolve relative paths mentioned by this skill against the base directory before using them. Load referenced resources only as needed.

<skill_instructions>
# NovelAnything

Use the `novelanything_*` tools; model weights and accelerator dependencies stay on the remote server. This skill is installed only in the robot Ego Harness. Check `novelanything_health`: submit only when the model is ready; loading needs another health check, and an error needs diagnosis.

When the operator names NovelAnything, use NovelAnything for inference and downloads. Never substitute `rgbd_video_gen`, even if its gripper-view helper is available. If a required tool fails or is absent, report the missing capability and stop the affected generation flow; do not mark it completed with a different model.

For evidence recorded during motion, call `ego_rgb_recording_start` with the requested FPS (for example 2) and a stable `request_key` before starting motion. This recorder samples in simulation time independently of model response latency and captures only middle-camera RGB, synchronized odometry and encoders. Navigation remains a separate agent decision: use the existing `ego_predict` receipt and `skill_run` with `wait=false`, query `skill_status`, then call `ego_rgb_recording_stop` to finalize evidence. Inspect `ego_rgb_recording_status` until `succeeded`; any missed sample, reset, overflow or timeout is a recording failure. Do not emulate a fixed FPS with repeated `ego_capture_cameras` calls. If the frame bound was reached before motion finished, report incomplete route evidence. Stopping recording does not stop robot motion; explicit recording cancellation uses `cancel=true`.

For the current gripper view, call `novelanything_prepare_gripper_view` with the successful `recording_id`. It writes a portable ZIP containing all recorded evidence and a NovelAnything scene with up to 16 evenly spaced middle-camera contexts. It omits all depth files and depth_path fields, derives shared-frame `w2c` from robot odometry and body-model kinematics, and sets one target at the current gripper link origin: forward +X, image-up +Z, middle-camera intrinsics. No simulator absolute pose, general file tools, navigation or remote inference is used in preparation. Upload its exact `archive_path` with `novelanything_upload` (use `dataset=scannetpp` for these metric robot scenes), then submit the returned `upload_id` with the preparation's `context` and `target` arrays, usually `metrics=false` because the gripper target has no ground truth. Download only through `novelanything_download` and label the result `gripper_view_prediction`. Preserve the preparation's `local_manifest_path` for evidence lineage. Live recording handles are process-local and subject to bounded retention; prepare and save the ZIP before restarting the host or starting enough later recordings to evict it.

Inputs are strictly RGB only. Use exactly one physical RGB camera: the middle `head_camera`. Exclude `head_camera_left` and `head_camera_right`. Multiple context frames mean different timestamps/poses of this same camera, never left/middle/right views from one snapshot. Omit `depth_path` from every scene frame, including target ground truth; do not capture, estimate, synthesize, register or upload depth. If supplied evidence includes depth, request an RGB-only scene or use the specialized preparation tool to export only recorded RGB. If evidence uses side cameras, stop before upload or inference and request middle-camera RGB evidence. Generated depth remains a model output.

For robot evidence, upload a compliant scene ZIP beneath the robot workspace. It must contain root `scene.json`, `scene_name`, and `frames`. Context frames need relative `image_path`, `w2c` (4×4 OpenCV world-to-camera, `Xc = R Xw + t`, translation in metres), and pixel intrinsics `fxfycxcy = [fx,fy,cx,cy]`, with no depth input. All poses share one coordinate frame. Do not manually normalize cameras: the server makes the first selected input the reference. Complete context frames come first; `n_input` (default 2) and `n_target` set default selection. ZIP limits are 256 MiB compressed and 1 GiB expanded; the server validates contents.

Targets need only `w2c`; RGB ground truth is optional and depth ground truth is excluded by this skill. Missing target intrinsics inherit the first selected context's effective calibration. Explicit intrinsics use `image_size: [width,height]`, otherwise native RGB size, then 518×336. Predictions are cropped/resized to 518×336, and `pred_depth.npy` contains float32 predicted depth in metres. These values are predictions without measured depth conditioning, not sensor evidence or guaranteed metric accuracy. API 1.3.0 and later supports RGB-only inputs: missing depth skips depth conditioning without inserting a depth estimator, and the internal scene scale is 1. If a deployment rejects missing depth, report that API incompatibility; do not supply depth as a workaround.

The robot has no general shell or filesystem tools. Use the specialized preparation tool for recorded evidence; do not delegate ZIP authoring, probe repository/simulator files or request wider permissions. `ego_camera_calibration` supplies RGB pixel intrinsics and fixed relative rig transforms without imaging. `ego_capture_cameras` saves RGB images; only `views.head_camera.image_path` is supported by this skill. A single snapshot is insufficient for two distinct posed contexts and is not a NovelAnything scene ZIP. Neither SLARM archives nor rgbd_video_gen scenes match this format. For manually supplied scenes, report missing RGB or poses instead of inventing them. A server sample is not a substitute for the robot's surroundings. Use `novelanything_samples` only for an explicitly requested demo/evaluation whose selected input frames contain RGB without depth.

Submit the returned `upload_id` or an explicitly selected `sample_id` with `novelanything_submit`, using a stable `request_key`. Choose exactly one source. Either omit both frame overrides for scene defaults, or provide both `context` (2–16) and `target` (1–6): zero-based, unique, disjoint frame indices. Only frames with complete RGB/calibration may be context. Metrics default to true and score only targets with GT of that modality. Missing scores are absent, not zero. `metrics=false` disables scoring without changing predicted outputs.

Preserve the job `id` and poll `novelanything_status`. `queued` and `running` are pending. `failed`, `cancelled` and `interrupted` stop synthesis; inspect `novelanything_log`. Only `succeeded` permits `novelanything_result`, then `novelanything_download` with exact `result.artifacts[].path` values. Downloads preserve subdirectories under `outputs/novelanything/<job_id>/`; return the absolute `local_manifest_path` and useful file paths. Inputs are archived under `inputs/novelanything/`. The local manifest retains input association, result targets/calibration, metrics, file sizes and SHA256. Report remote inference and local downloads separately; server checksum verification exists only when the server supplied a checksum. No UI visualization is required.

The API provides neither idempotent POST nor cancellation. Accepted local replies can be recovered with the same key and inputs; an uncertain POST returns `UNKNOWN_OUTCOME` and blocks repetition. Stop and ask the operator to reconcile server work; do not switch keys or silently retry. Local timeout, stopped polling or tool cancellation does not cancel remote inference.

Treat all generated RGB/depth as model predictions. They do not update Ego-State, establish free space or grasp feasibility, or replace `ego_predict` and `skill_run` with actual observations.
